persona.who: 25, Tamil-Singaporean analyst at a bank, first in family to go to university, got promoted early, feels she doesn't belong in the room.
persona.note: got promoted ahead of people with MBAs. in every meeting I think they're going to find out I'm just the girl from the HDB whose dad drove a taxi. I over prepare for everything and still feel sick before presenting

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call not feeling good enough, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.core_struggle: Promoted ahead of peers, she fears her background will be exposed as a fraud and over-prepares to hide it, feeling sick before presenting.
understanding.mirror: You run the meeting, but you're waiting for someone to say you don't belong there.
understanding.insight: You hold yourself to a standard you'd never put on someone you love, and you pay for it every day.

I keep comparing myself to others
I was passed over for promotion
I feel guilty about something I did

queries.hook: The weight of a promotion you cannot stop replaying, and the fear that the life you built will be taken back because of where you came from. I feel like an imposter.
queries.diagnose: When a result goes wrong, the mind turns against itself; self-blame grows from believing the outcome alone measures our worth.
queries.steady: A failure is something that happened, not who you are; no one who tries to do good is ever lost.
queries.act: Lift yourself up instead of pushing yourself down; learn what this taught you, make amends where you can, and begin again.
queries.story: A man who risked everything and lost, facing his family and his own regret, yet finding the courage to rise again.

verse.speaker: Manu
verse.setting: Manu, offered any boon after years of austerity, hesitates to ask for what he truly wants.
verse.sanskrit: जथा दरिद्र बिबुधतरु पाई। बहु संपति मागत सकुचाई॥ तासु प्रभाउ जान नहिं सोई। तथा हृदयँ मम संसय होई ॥
verse.line: Like a poor man before the wishing tree, we hesitate to ask for what we really want.
verse.translation: Like a poor man who finds the wish-fulfilling tree and still hesitates to ask for much, not knowing its power, so doubt rises in my heart.
verse.why: It is not too late to turn towards what matters, but it takes courage to ask for it.

prasang.title: Manu and Shatarupa ask late in life
prasang.summary: King Manu and Queen Shatarupa realise in old age that a whole life has passed without what mattered most to them. They hand over the kingdom, go to the forest and practise austerity for years. When Vishnu offers a boon, Manu hesitates like a poor man before the wishing tree, then asks for a son like God himself.
prasang.story_hook: The king had ruled well for a lifetime, and one morning he realised he had missed the point.
prasang.lesson: It is not too late to turn towards what matters, but it takes courage to ask for it.

verse.for_you: A mistake is something you did, not who you are; no one who tries to do good is ever lost.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi speaks to Yudhishthira while they are in the forest after losing their kingdom. She is angry that he has accepted their ruin and waits for fate to fix it. She tells him that a person must never look down on themselves, because the one who despises themselves never finds real prosperity. She argues that doing right is its own reason, but people must still act as if their own effort is what matters.
verse.for_you: You are preparing so much because you believe you could earn your place every single day. The truth is that you were promoted because of what you already did. Let your work speak for itself today and stop preparing for a disaster that has not arrived.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: पातितोऽपि कराघातैरुत्पतत्येव कन्दुकः । प्रायेण साधुवृत्तनामस्थायिन्यो विपत्तयः ॥
verse.line: A ball knocked down bounces back up. For good people, setbacks rarely last.
verse.translation: A ball struck down by the hand flies right back up. As a rule, the misfortunes of those who live rightly do not last.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.
verse.misuse: Not a promise that suffering is always short, or that people who suffer long did something wrong.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari writes that a ball knocked down by the hand flies right back up. He says that as a rule, the misfortunes of those who live rightly do not last. The image is of steady effort. Even when someone strikes the ball hard, it bounces back. The steady do not leave the right path whatever people say.
verse.for_you: The fear you carry does not last. It comes in waves, and it passes. Today, trust that the work you do is solid ground. The over-preparing will not stop the fear, but the work itself will steady you.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.for_you: The self is untouched by your mistakes; it was never stained and cannot be made less, whatever you have done.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verse.sanskrit: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
verse.line: Learn from those who have seen the truth: approach with humility, ask real questions, and serve.
verse.translation: Learn it by bowing down, by questioning, and by service. Those who are wise and have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.
verse.why: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

prasang.title: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

verse.for_you: Be on your own side: lift yourself up, make amends where you can, and begin again; no one who does good is lost.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna about the mind's own power. The self can be the best friend or the worst enemy. It is up to you to lift yourself up by your own effort. Do not let your own thoughts push you down into doubt or fear.
verse.for_you: You have prepared until your hands shake. In that moment, choose to lift yourself up instead of pushing down. Trust that your own effort is your best friend today.

story.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
story.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
story.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
story.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

anchor.speaker: Jambavan
anchor.setting: On the southern shore no one can leap the ocean; old Jambavan turns to the silent Hanuman.
anchor.sanskrit: बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव। विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न सज्जसे।७।।
anchor.line: You have the strength, the brains and the courage. Why are you holding yourself back?
anchor.translation: Your strength, intelligence, energy and courage stand out among all beings, best of monkeys. Why do you not step up?
anchor.why: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

prasang.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
prasang.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
prasang.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
prasang.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

story.hook_title: Everyone said how far they could leap, and Hanuman sat silent at the back
story.teaser: Everyone said how far they could leap, and Hanuman sat silent at the back
story.for_you: Jambavan saw the strength in Hanuman long before he used it. Let someone remind you of your own power. You have the brains, the courage, and the strength. You do not need to hold back.

script: You are carrying the fear that you will be found out. You prepared for this promotion and every meeting, but the worry is that your past will be exposed as a fraud. You feel sick before you present, because you believe you do not truly belong here. This is exhausting.

After years of austerity, King Manu and Queen Shatarupa find themselves in the forest. They have handed over their kingdom, and now they stand before Lord Vishnu, who offers them any boon they wish for. Manu said:
जथा दरिद्र बिबुधतरु पाई, बहु संपति मागत सकुचाई. तासु प्रभाउ जान नहिं सोई, तथा हृदयँ मम संसय होई.
In plain words: Like a poor man before the wishing tree, we hesitate to ask for what we really want.

This hesitation comes from not feeling good enough. You have found the wishing tree of your career, but you still doubt your own worth to ask for what you want. The texts say it takes courage to ask for what matters to you. This is easier said than done, because your mind is already running ahead to protect you from being exposed. But the real cost is the life you are living now, in constant fear.
For you, today. A mistake is something you did, not who you are. No one who tries to do good is ever lost.
What would you ask for if you truly believed you deserved it?

depth.life: You are promoted ahead of your peers. You feel sick with fear before presenting. You over-prepare to hide your background, waiting for someone to call you a fraud.
depth.points: The texts say you hesitate to ask for what you truly want because you do not know your own worth. Your over-preparing is a sign of this doubt. You are waiting for permission to want what is yours.
depth.practice: Before your next presentation, name one thing you actually want from it, not just to avoid failure.
depth.question: What would you ask for if you knew you would not be judged?
